subject: Edge connector partition — immediate routing guidance and post-incident actions
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Atlas Retail Ops <ops@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-09T07:15:00Z
Subject: Edge connector partition — immediate reroute steps (US & follow-on guidance)

Hi Ben / Atlas ops team,

Quick update and immediate actions: we detected a partition between our edge connector fleet and a major cloud backbone affecting traffic destined for the US region (some EU/APAC customers also saw elevated tail latency). The incident is impacting a subset of connections to us-east and us-west endpoints; we are actively mitigating.

What to do now (recommended, low-risk):
1) Prefer explicit region routing: add header X-Redwood-Region: us-west-1 or use the query parameter ?region=us-west-1 in API calls. Example: 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "X-Redwood-Region: us-west-1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n    -d '{"model":"redwood-2.1","prompt":"ping"}'

2) Fallback endpoint: switch to the regional fallback host api.us-west.redwood.ai (this host accepts the same auth and tokens). We expect this to restore normal latency for most customers.

3) Short-term model variant: if you see token errors/timeouts, set model=redwood-2.1-mini or model=redwood-2.1-quant as a temporary fallback (lower memory, more tolerant to routing retries).

Attached is a one-page reroute-checklist.csv with a step-by-step checklist and verification commands. If you’d like, I can loop in an engineer to apply this with you.

Known impact and ETA: we’ve isolated the backbone peer and applied a traffic shift; most customers who switched region preference report immediate improvement. Our infra team estimates a full remediation and verification window of ~36 hours. We’ll post updates to https://status.redwood.ai and follow up with a post-incident note.

If you confirm when you’ve applied the header/endpoint swap, I’ll mark you as recovered and we’ll keep monitoring.

Sincerely,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: reroute-checklist.csv, customer-facing-sample-email.txt

From: Ben Kline <ben.kline@atlasretail.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-09T07:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Edge connector partition — immediate reroute steps (US & follow-on guidance)

Thanks Sofia — we applied the X-Redwood-Region header on our staging and started routing traffic to api.us-west.redwood.ai. Latency dropped from ~700ms to ~120ms for our test calls.

One question: will changing to the fallback host affect our billing/quotas or model pinning? We have some pinned model versions for production.

—Ben
Ops Lead, Atlas Retail

On 2026-11-09 07:15, Sofia Ivanova wrote:
> Quick update and immediate actions: we detected a partition between our edge connector fleet and a major cloud backbone affecting traffic destined for the US region (some EU/APAC customers also saw elevated tail latency).

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-09T08:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Edge connector partition — internal follow-up

Sofia / Rishi — brief internal notes and action items.
1) Root cause: our telemetry indicates a sustained BGP flap at a regional carrier peer between us-east POP and one colo; packets were blackholed for sessions that had an existing TCP 3-way handshake. This explains why reconnects to fallback endpoints worked.
2) Immediate mitigation = confirmed: traffic-shift policy deployed at the router-plane (20% -> 100% to alternate peers), and regional host api.us-west.redwood.ai is stable.
3) Customer comms: Sofia — recommend we send a follow-up postmortem to impacted accounts with: timeline, RCA (high-level), mitigation, and permanent mitigations planned (peer replacements + active-health checks + automatic region-fallback at the client-side). Also offer one month of service credit for customers with SLA impact.
4) Ops ask for Rishi: please grab network traces from the affected POP (attached network-trace-20261109.zip) and create a short runbook for SREs to rehome sessions without requiring client reconnect.

I’ll update the status page and draft the public postmortem once we have Rishi’s traces.

Laura
Director, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

On 2026-11-09 07:15, Sofia Ivanova wrote:
> Attached is a one-page reroute-checklist.csv with a step-by-step checklist and verification commands.

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Atlas Retail Ops <ops@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-11T10:42:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: post-incident summary and next steps (Edge connector partition)

Hi Ben —

Thank you again for working with us during the incident. This is a short post-incident summary and the actions we’ve taken since your confirmation on 11/09.

Summary: on 2026-11-09 at ~06:50 UTC a regional carrier experienced a routing instability that caused a partition between a Redwood edge POP and several cloud backhaul peers. Impact: elevated tail latency and occasional failed connections for a subset of customers routing through the affected POPs (primarily US). We mitigated by shifting traffic to alternate peers and providing an explicit regional endpoint for immediate relief.

What we did for you:
- Confirmed successful reroute to api.us-west.redwood.ai and verified latency improvements.
- Reviewed your pinned-model config; switching to the fallback host does not change billing rates or your model pin; quotas remain the same. We honored identical rate limits on the fallback host during the incident.
- Per Laura’s note, we are extending one month of service credit to Atlas Retail due to measurable SLA degradation. I’ve opened HS-987654 in HubSpot to track the credit and approval flow.

Technical artifacts attached: network-trace-20261109.zip (SRE traces), reroute-checklist.csv (customer steps), and a short customer-facing template you can use for internal teams (customer-facing-sample-email.txt).

Next steps and timeline:
- Short term (completed): traffic shift and regional endpoint support (done 11/09).
- Medium term (2–4 weeks): replace the affected carrier peering in the US colo and add automated health-check failover at the POP level.
- Long term (Q1): add client-side SDK support for automatic region-failover and a persistent connection rehome mechanism.

If you’d like a 30-minute technical review with our SREs to walk through the traces and confirm your rollout, we can schedule that this week. Please reply with times that work.

Apologies for the disruption and thanks for the fast collaboration.

Best regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: reroute-checklist.csv, network-trace-20261109.zip, customer-facing-sample-email.txt
